display.purpose: Rajdhani 700. One h1 per page in .page-heading. Condensed departure-board authority.

headline.purpose: Rajdhani 600, 1.35rem. Section and docket headings. Carries its own weight — no explainer paragraph beneath.

body.purpose: Fira Sans 400/1.6. Operator prose, capped at 68ch.

label.purpose: JetBrains Mono 500, uppercase, 0.15em (--track-label). Field labels, dt terms, ledger column heads.

data.purpose: JetBrains Mono 400. Machine facts: timestamps, URLs, digests, formats. Tabular figures wherever a number can change width.

tally.purpose: Rajdhani 600, tabular. Percentages, folios, per-row counts.

shadows.name: shadow-panel
shadows.purpose: Ambient atmosphere under every docket, station, plate and gate. Constant at rest and on hover — never a state signal.

shadows.name: shadow-island
shadows.purpose: The mobile navigation island only, paired with backdrop-filter: blur(18px) saturate(1.3).

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The system's only easing curve, inherited from Shoreline. Every transition and reveal uses it.

motion.name: dur-hover
motion.purpose: Colour, border and ground move together on hover. No lift, no scale-up, no shadow change.

motion.name: sweep-step
motion.purpose: The diagonal flip-dot reveal, a ~670ms crossing from the top-left. Quantised into classes because the CSP forbids inline per-dot delays.

motion.name: signal-breathe
motion.purpose: The background dot lattice. Frozen entirely (animation: none) under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: island
breakpoints.purpose: The hairline section rail becomes the floating island navigation; grids collapse to one column; the job ledger becomes a stack of records.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Panel padding trims to --s6, wordmark sub-line hides, flipdot-lg shrinks.

breakpoints.name: coarse
breakpoints.purpose: Orthogonal to width: 52px minimum row height, 32px minimum for small standalone links.

breakpoints.name: reduced-motion
breakpoints.purpose: Signal field and every flip dot get animation-name: none; transforms are removed, not shortened.

narrative.overview:
Sources arrive off the open network and are filed onto a shelf, and the whole interface is the departure board that reports on it. An electromechanical flip-dot board states the floor in one word, monospaced data runs in registers beneath it, condensed display type carries the headings, and structure is drawn with hairline rules rather than stacked cards. This is an operator tool for one self-hoster, so it is dense, quiet and legible at a glance, with exactly one loud object per surface.

The world is a mesh of two existing systems, not an invention. Dark is Shoreline's ocean: a #0a161e page, foam-teal accent, a black dot board, hairline panels sitting under the page colour rather than raised above it. Light is streetCryptid's daybreak: cool off-white paper at #eef2f5, #152633 ink, #d6dee4 hairlines, and a dot board rendered in dark ink because a pale teal dot cannot hold 4.5:1 against paper. Both come from one token set: every themed value is a light-dark() pair and color-scheme on :root is the only switch, so the OS preference works with zero JavaScript.

Two hard constraints shaped everything. The CSP has no unsafe-inline (script-src 'self', style-src 'self', font-src 'self'), so there is no inline style attribute, no inline script and no CDN font anywhere — which is why the flip-dot board quantises per-dot colour and delay into class names, why three typefaces are self-hosted woff2 latin subsets, and why job progress is a real <progress> element. And there is no npm or Node build step: htmx is vendored and every page is server-rendered Razor.
keyCharacteristics: Two themes, one token set, switched by color-scheme — no JavaScript required for correctness.
Every edge is a hairline; structure comes from rules, never from a nested card.
One accent hue family (the ocean ramp) plus amber as an attention rim, never an identity.
The flip-dot board is the only loud element, and there is one per surface.
No inline styles anywhere: per-dot colour and delay are quantised into class names.
Status never rests on colour alone — every mark sits beside the state's word.
The same nav markup is a hairline rail on desktop and a floating island under 62rem.

rules.name: The One Hue Rule
rules.body: The palette is one ocean hue family plus amber. A new colour is not added; a new role is expressed by re-pitching the existing accent (--accent-quiet, --accent-line, --accent-wash) or by the semantic trio. Amber never becomes an identity colour.

rules.name: The Word-Beside-the-Mark Rule
rules.body: Status never rests on colour alone. Every .status-mark sits next to the state's word, and the flip-dot board renders the state as literal letters. A colour-only indicator is not a state.

rules.name: The Retargeting Rule
rules.body: No component hardcodes a hex. Every themed value is a light-dark() pair declared once on :root. The only literals below the token layer are button-primary's two contrast partners, light-dark(#ffffff, #04141b).

rules.name: The Three-Voice Rule
rules.body: Rajdhani speaks headings and numbers, JetBrains Mono speaks machine facts, Fira Sans speaks to the operator. A label is never set in the sans face and a paragraph is never set in mono; .field-check and .action-form h4 revert to sans on purpose because they address a person.

rules.name: The Heading-Carries-Itself Rule
rules.body: A section heading does not get an explanatory paragraph restating it. .section-heading p exists for a mono sub-fact — a count, a filter state — not for an explainer.

rules.name: The One Navigation Rule
rules.body: There is one nav element in the document and it changes shape, not identity. No second mobile nav, no hamburger, no duplicated landmark for a screen reader to walk twice.

rules.name: The No-Lift Rule
rules.body: Hover moves colour, border and ground together: no translateY, no scale-up, no shadow change. Two small transforms exist and neither is a lift — .button:active { transform: scale(0.98) } and .book-row:hover .row-arrow { transform: translateX(2px) } — and both are removed under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Hairline-Not-Nesting Rule
rules.body: A panel gets structure from rules, not from another card. Nested cards are banned. Where a station board sits inside a docket it sheds border, radius, background and shadow and keeps a hairline — and drops even that when it is :last-child, because a clear floor has no list to divide.

rules.name: The Sanctioned Character Rule
rules.body: Iconography is two-part, because the mesh has two halves. Navigation and controls use drawn SVG: 24 viewBox, stroke-width 1.6, fill none, currentColor (streetCryptid's half). Row affordances and inline direction use Shoreline's permitted characters and only those: › and ‹ for chevrons, · for the metadata separator, — / – for dashes — Shoreline's web half ships no icon set and names › as its entry chevron. No other Unicode stands in for an icon and no emoji appears anywhere; a character used this way is always aria-hidden and never the only carrier of meaning.

rules.name: The Reserved Rule
rules.body: The 2px accent left-rule belongs to the inset Card (.action-form) and to nothing else. Notices, callouts and alerts are hairline boxes with a tinted ground.

dos: Do declare every new themed value as a light-dark() pair on :root in bindery.css, so color-scheme stays the single switch and the no-JavaScript path stays correct.
Do carry structure with hairlines: --hairline for panel edges and section rules, --hairline-soft between rows, --hairline-strong for control borders and the dashed empty state.
Do put a word beside every state mark, and prefer the flip-dot board when a surface needs to state one status.
Do keep hover to colour + border + ground, transitioned over 200ms with cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) — the system's only easing curve.

Do draw navigation and control icons as inline 24-viewBox SVG at stroke-width 1.6, fill none, in currentColor — and use › / ‹ / · for row affordances, pager direction and metadata separation, aria-hidden in every case.
Do give real elements their semantics: <progress> for progress, <time>/<data> for values, role="img" plus aria-label for a board.
Do freeze motion under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce — animation: none on both .signal-field and every .fd, not merely a shorter duration.
Do hold WCAG AA on both themes, composited against the actual ancestor ground including alpha washes.
Do treat the --bnd-* properties and .bnd-* classes as a versioned protocol contract with plugins (docs/PLUGIN-UI.md rule 3).
donts: Don't write an inline style attribute, an inline <script>, or a CDN font link — the CSP has no unsafe-inline, which is also why the htmx-config meta disables htmx's injected indicator styles.
Don't nest a card inside a card; strip the inner thing's chrome down to a hairline the way .queue-docket > .station does.
Don't put the 2px accent left-rule on a notice, callout or alert; it is reserved for the inset Card (.action-form).
Don't lift, scale up, or change a shadow on hover.
Don't use a glow or a colour shift as the focus indicator; focus is a hard 2px ring at 4px offset.
Don't press any other Unicode character into service as an icon — no arrows, no bullets beyond ·, no emoji, no icon font. Outside the sanctioned set, an icon is drawn SVG or it does not exist.
Don't repeat a fact the board already stated — on a clear floor the sub-line and the job list disappear rather than echoing CLEAR.
Don't add an explanatory paragraph under a section heading.
Don't introduce a second accent hue, or promote amber from an attention rim to an identity colour.
